body:
Since `AT TIME ZONE` on a `TIMESTAMP_NS` returns a `TIMESTAMPTZ_NS`, comparing the result with a `TIMESTAMPTZ` fails to bind, while `TIMESTAMP_NS` and `TIMESTAMP` compare fine:

```sql
SELECT (TIMESTAMP_NS '2026-10-12 12:34:56.123456789' AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') < now();
-- Binder Error: Cannot compare values of type TIMESTAMPTZ_NS and type TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE - an explicit cast is required
```

The same happens for `BETWEEN`, `COALESCE`, `IN` and list literals that mix the two. They combine the types through an implicit cast in one direction, and `CastRules::ImplicitCast` has no rule for a `TIMESTAMP_TZ` source, so neither direction is allowed.

This allows `TIMESTAMP_TZ` to `TIMESTAMP_TZ_NS`, as `TIMESTAMP` already casts implicitly to `TIMESTAMP_NS`, so the microsecond side is cast up. On #28039 the different ranges of the two types came up as the reason against this cast. `TIMESTAMP` and `TIMESTAMP_NS` differ in the same way, and a `TIMESTAMPTZ` outside the nanosecond range now fails with the same "Could not convert Timestamp to higher precision" that a `TIMESTAMP` gets today. The cast also lets a `TIMESTAMPTZ` argument bind to an overload that only takes `TIMESTAMPTZ_NS`, such as a `date_diff` that mixes the two.

If that is acceptable, as a v2.0 regression, could this get the `backport v2.0-cyanoptera` label?

review_comments.body: I know this has been merged but in future it would be good to use non-UTC time zones for testing.
review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+# name: test/sql/types/timestamp/timestamptz_ns_timestamptz_comparison.test
+# description: TIMESTAMPTZ_NS combines with TIMESTAMPTZ at nanosecond precision, as TIMESTAMP_NS does with TIMESTAMP
+# group: [timestamp]
+
+require icu
+
+statement ok
+SET TimeZone = 'UTC';

title: Compare TIMESTAMPTZ_NS with TIMESTAMPTZ without an explicit cast
